question: The Mahabodhi Temple, a UNESCO World Heritage site is in which of the following state?
solution: The correct answer is __**Bihar**__. [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__** • **The Mahabodhi Temple** is located in **Bodh Gaya, Bihar**, India, and is one of the most sacred pilgrimage sites for Buddhists worldwide. • It was declared a **UNESCO World Heritage Site** in **2002** due to its immense religious, historical, and architectural significance. • The temple marks the location where **Lord Buddha attained enlightenment** under the sacred Bodhi tree around the 6th century BCE. • The original structure was built by Emperor **Ashoka** in the **3rd century BCE**, and the current temple is believed to date back to the 5th–6th century CE. • The temple complex includes the **Mahabodhi Stupa**, the Bodhi Tree, the Vajrasana (Diamond Throne), and several smaller stupas and shrines around the main temple.
